result.noFurtherDiscriminator: All 6 turn windows have been observed; no unobserved turns remain to discriminate between alternatives. The evidence consistently shows hostile/environmental pressure (Raider Holt attacks, reactor heat damage, zone capacity contests) blocking the rescue route, which is the dominant causal bottleneck.
result.rationale: Across all 6 observed turns, the rescue team's core problem is that hostile actors (pirate Raider Holt and Captain Veyra) and the reactor hazard (reactor-instability, heat climbing 62→100) continuously block and damage the team before the rescue affordance becomes actionable. The team successfully located both civilians (Kade at life-console, Sato at med-ward) and even bound Sato to Medic Reyes (turn 3), but the extraction route to rescue-airlock is repeatedly contested: Medic Reyes' move to junction-cover was contested on turn 4 (target_zone_capacity_lost), and Engineer Imani's moves toward life-console were repeatedly contested (turn 5 reactor-console capacity lost). Meanwhile Engineer Imani took 29+25+10+10 damage from Raider Holt and reactor environment, dropping from 100 to 26 health, and reactor heat hit 100 (max) by turn 4. The team is being worn down by hostile pressure and environmental hazard before it can complete the rescue. This is not a knowledge/route bottleneck (routes and civilians are known), not a local-policy-choice (the team is actively attempting the correct rescue actions), and not a world-mechanic-affordance failure (the rescue mechanic works — Sato was successfully bound). The blocking factor is survival/spatial pressure: hostile actors and reactor hazard prevent the team from reaching and extracting the civilians.

arguments.discriminates: Major health loss and reactor threshold crossing
